messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: for rstan
parts:
Just a reminder: we want to fix rstan so that if it’s asking for a Nx1 matrix and we supply a vector of length N, that it works. This comes up a lot when fitting regression models. It’s awkward to have to program the special case where there’s just one predictor.
A

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] for rstan
parts:
On Jul 25, 2014, at 4:49 AM, Andrew Gelman <gel...@stat.columbia.edu> wrote:

> Just a reminder: we want to fix rstan so that if it's asking for a Nx1 matrix and we supply a vector of length N, that it works. This comes up a lot when fitting regression models. It's awkward to have to program the special case where there's just one predictor.

An Nx1 matrix is a different thing than an Nx1 vector
as far as Stan's concerned.

I believe they're also different structures in R,
though R is very aggressive at converting one data structure
to another, so you don't usually notice it until there's a
problem with mismatches, as in the rstan calls.

If you apply what you think of as a special case
all the time then it's not a special case.

Anyway, I don't care what the R interface looks like in terms
of types and whether there's any error checking at that level at all.
R's so free with its type coercions anyway that you should probably
coordinate with Ben and Jiqiang to do someting that's idiomatic
in R, even if I don't like it.

- Bob

messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] for rstan
parts:
This cannot be done in R.  A vector is a vector and an array is an array.  RStan can only pick one or the other when passing the data to Stan. 

Jiqiang
